newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate falls back to 9.7 vs 11 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate falls back to 9.7 vs 11 pct.

text.p: Croatia's money market average rate fell back to 9.7 percent on Thursday from 11 percent after banks cut some rates as demand for kuna shrank.
Dealers said trade totalled 13.5 million kuna, leaving more than 30 million surplus on the supply side.
Insurers' offer was left untouched as deposits at commercial banks rose significantly, they said.
The one-month rate fell to 12 percent from 15, charged for some loans on Wednesday. One-week interbank funds were granted at 10 percent and call money at an unchanged 9.0 percent.
Only 330,000 kuna were settled in Wednesday's overnight trade, compared to 20 million a day earlier.
The central bank said it still had no operations although its board approved some foreign exchange purchases this month.
It calculated the kuna midrates for Friday weaker at 5.5635 versus 5.5524 to the dollar and 3.5634 against the German mark. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
